snippet.title: Hitler's invasion of the Soviet Union: Operation Barbarossa (1/2) | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
On 22 June 1941, the German Wehrmacht launched a war of aggression against the Soviet Union. Under the code name ‘Operation Barbarossa’, the campaign aimed to bring the vast country in the east to its knees. Millions of people died as a result.

At the beginning of the Second World War, the Nazi regime celebrated a series of military successes: boosted by rapid victories in Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium and France, the Wehrmacht prepared a secret maneuver in the east, firmly convinced that troops would be back home after a few months. But the period of unimaginable violence unleashed by Hitler would claim millions of lives.

Without declaring war and with more than three million soldiers battle-ready, the Wehrmacht attacked on a broad front between the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea. In the first hours of the meticulously prepared military invasion, the Luftwaffe rained bombs on Soviet bases near the border, catching the Soviets completely off-guard.

The force of the attack was seen as a continuation of the German troops’ successful ‘Blitzkrieg’ campaigns. In his instructions to the Chief of Operations in the Armed Forces High Command, written in March 1941, Hitler had already stated: ‘This upcoming campaign is more than just a battle of arms, it’s also a clash between two worldviews. The Jewish-Bolshevik intelligentsia, as the previous oppressor of the people, must be eliminated.’

Another aim: the economic exploitation of conquered territories. Many of those involved and affected by this tragedy - Germans and Soviets, soldiers and civilians alike - recorded their harrowing experiences in amateur films, letters and diaries. These vivid descriptions of the German war of aggression in the East are a far cry from official war reporting and state propaganda. These accounts, by men and women fighting for survival, document the horror on both sides of the conflict.

snippet.title: Richard Hammond's Wild Weather: Temperature: The Driving Force
snippet.description:
Unlock the mysteries of weather—see the powerful science behind lightning, snow, dust storms, and more in this jaw-dropping exploration of Earth's most amazing forces.

Join us as we dive deep into the astonishing world of weather, revealing how simple ingredients—wind, water, and temperature—combine to create everything from gentle clouds to raging dust storms and wild lightning strikes. Through ambitious and sometimes wild experiments, we strip weather back to basics, uncovering the secret science behind everyday wonders and extreme phenomena alike.

Discover how rising thermals lift rain into the sky, why desert dust can travel thousands of miles to seed rain in distant lands, and the crucial role dust plays in creating rainfall itself. Watch as freezing rain encases everything it touches in clear ice, and learn the surprising science of snowflake formation and transformation. Journey to places where we recreate the drama of thundering lightning storms, witnessing how temperature controls everything from fog on the ground to the deafening shockwaves of thunder in the air.

This video breaks down complex weather patterns—like why fog is white, how clouds darken before a storm, and why no two snowflakes are ever alike—into simple, visual, and unforgettable demonstrations. Whether you're curious about the everyday rain on your car, the epic power of thunderstorms, or the delicate artistry of frost, this episode reveals the extraordinary secrets hidden in the sky above us.

snippet.title: Richard Hammond's Wild Weather: Water: The Shape Shifter
snippet.description:
Discover the astonishing science behind water and weather, from heavy clouds to powerful avalanches—explained with amazing experiments and real-life demonstrations!

Unravel the secrets of Earth’s most dynamic force—weather—as we break down how water creates the fastest, slowest, softest, and hardest weather on the planet. Dive inside clouds to see just how much they weigh, learn the real difference between rain, drizzle, hail, sleet, and ice pellets, and witness wild experiments—including weighing a cloud with a helicopter, smashing water on a car, and firing artificial hail at high speeds!

Explore how seemingly gentle snow can become a deadly avalanche, how raindrops are formed through coalescence, and why hail is so powerful. We’ll even build homemade clouds, watch avalanches race down mountains, and answer mind-blowing questions—like what would happen if all the rain fell at once? Perfect for science lovers and anyone who’s ever wondered how the weather really works, this deep dive into meteorology blends hands-on experiments with clear explanations of complex processes.

snippet.title: Trump’s Inner Circle & Use of Military Power | The War Cabinet (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
A 90-minute documentary examining the key players behind President Trump’s expansive use of the U.S. military during his second term. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

When Donald Trump campaigned for his second term, he made a repeated promise: no new wars.

Drawing on in-depth interviews with President Trump’s allies and associates, officials from his first administration, and his critics, as well as former diplomats, military experts and journalists, “The War Cabinet” traces how, after vowing to end wars, not start them, Trump assembled a team of loyalists, and together they pursued a much different course. 

That team includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, longtime aide Stephen Miller, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Vice President JD Vance and outgoing Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. The documentary tells the story of how the cabinet, a group whose members had diverse life stories and worldviews, came together to support the president in his quest to demonstrate the United States’ military might on the international stage.

The film traces how Trump has increasingly sought to cement his legacy and achieve U.S. policy objectives through military strength; how the administration has engaged militarily everywhere from Yemen, to the waters off Venezuela, to Iran; and the roles of key players in Trump’s second-term military decisions. With the Iran conflict now in its third month and threatening to define Trump’s second term, “The War Cabinet” is a must-watch documentary on how the president who promised peace has become a wartime president — and the ongoing ramifications.

snippet.title: Born in Bethlehem - Between checkpoints and the delivery room in the West Bank | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
These are the stories of women giving birth at the hospital in Bethlehem. The Holy Family Hospital is a place of hope, in a region marked by conflict, violence and insecurity.

The film offers an intimate glimpse into the daily lives of the doctors, midwives and nurses who fight with unwavering dedication for the health of mothers and newborns. Bethlehem, the biblical birthplace of Jesus, lies at the heart of a region that has been a battleground for decades. This makes the work of the hospital run by the Order of Malta all the more significant: Since 1990, more than 100,000 children have been born there. The facility provides medical care of the highest standard - regardless of the expectant mothers’ origin, religion or social status. A mobile medical team also travels to remote villages around Bethlehem, often under difficult conditions, passing through checkpoints and roadblocks.

The documentary follows expectant mothers and the dedicated staff. One of them is gynecologist Dana Amro. "We open our doors to all pregnant women - regardless of gender, religion or skin color. We turn away no one who asks us for help,” she says. Amro often has to set off for work extremely early, in order to allow for any potential delays on the way.

Senior midwife Lorette Farah Khalil Al-Allam has been working at Holy Family Hospital for 27 years and has attended thousands of births. Among the mothers featured is Khuloud Obayat, who lost her husband shortly before the birth of her son Omar and is raising her children in difficult circumstances.

Despite all the tensions in the region, the maternity hospital sends out a powerful message of humanity, solidarity and active compassion. Whilst in many places people are asking how peace can be possible, this place provides a clear answer - with an open door, and open hearts.

snippet.title: Pablo Escobar’s Rise & Fall | The Godfather of Cocaine (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the bloody rise and fall of Pablo Escobar and how the empire he built set the stage for the modern narco-trafficking industry. (Aired 1995)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

This archival FRONTLINE documentary examines how one drug, cocaine, began flowing into the U.S. at an industrial scale in the 1970s and 1980s — and the pivotal role of the notorious Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar, the boss of the Medellin cocaine cartel. 

With remarkable access to Escobar’s family, relatives of his victims, and both Colombian and U.S. officials, “The Godfather of Cocaine” traces how Escobar built a multi-billion-dollar fortune through international cocaine smuggling alliances and a sophisticated operation to traffic cocaine into the U.S.

Escobar maintained his dominance through violent repression and extreme brutality, with his cartel funneling drug profits into attacks and killings that brought Colombia to a state of virtual civil war. 

Colombian police and the U.S. DEA hunted Escobar down and assassinated him in 1993, but it didn’t end the narco-trafficking model he built. 

“The death of Escobar was a landmark in the history of an industry, but it wasn't a victory, in the sense that it didn’t put anything out of business,” Senate investigator Jack Blum said in the documentary. “It didn't change the pace of trafficking. It didn't raise or lower the price of cocaine.”

“The Godfather of Cocaine” was produced by William Cran and Stephanie Tepper. The associate producers were Christopher Buchanan and Marcela Gaviria. The documentary was written and directed by William Cran. Cran, a prolific and acclaimed documentary filmmaker, passed away in 2025: https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/remembering-william-cran-prolific-and-acclaimed-documentary-filmmaker/

snippet.description:
Water made life on Earth possible and shaped the rise of human civilization. From the first rivers that nurtured ancient societies to the vast oceans regulating the planet’s climate, water has always been the foundation of life. From melting glaciers and rising sea levels to droughts and freshwater shortages, this episode of Anthropocene reveals how humans are reshaping one of Earth’s most vital systems and what that means for the future of the planet.

snippet.title: The Luxury Call Girl Murder: Power, Money and Lies | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
It is the 1st November 1957 when the police open a flat in Frankfurt's Stiftstraße and smell an acrid odour. It emanates from the living room. There she lies - the 24-year-old luxury call girl Rosemarie Nitribitt. 
Her death hits like a bomb in the middle of the economic miracle of the 1950s. Nitribitt is not just anyone. She is both a sensation and a provocation. Rosemarie Nitribitt, always elegantly dressed, goes out in public with a black Mercedes convertible and a white poodle to catch customers. But not where other prostitutes wait for clients. Rosemarie Nitribitt also attracts male company from the noble hotels, who are only too happy to use her services. Nitribitt is traded under the table among the moneyed aristocracy as a kind of trophy. However, her murderer was never found. Cold Case reopens the case.
